items.title: Branford Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I started listening to that Ornette Coleman record in eighty-four that Crouch gave me.

ctx.x: I wasn’t really listening to Bird. I’d learned a couple of solos. I wasn’t really listening to Bird. But I was into the Wayne Shorter thing at that time, so I didn’t get to it at that time. But it was duly noted. It was duly noted. I got it. I’m going to have to get to this. And then Wynton left and started his band and I still didn’t get to it, but I kept hitting these walls. I

was cognizant of the fact that I was basically repeating myself every other bar and playing the same shit over and over again and I just didn’t have enough information. I started listening to that Ornette Coleman record in eighty-four that Crouch gave me.
The Shape of Jazz to Come?
